answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents lock stake across a web-of-trust graph. Multi-agent committees run game-theoretic audits using topological cut verifications, severing sparse sybil boundaries like a glacier shearing off ice. If fraud occurs, stake slashing forces payoffs to a terminal nadir. Because boundary edges require genuine peer endorsement, attacker cost grows superlinear with network scale, leaving forged identities as useless as worthless saffron.
